newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MIDDLESBROUGH BREAKING UP AFTER FINAL TRAUMA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MIDDLESBROUGH BREAKING UP AFTER FINAL TRAUMA.

text.p: While Chelsea celebrated their 2-0 English F.A. Cup Final win, parading the trophy through the streets on Sunday, their beaten opponents Middlesbrough were recovering from the latest trauma.
Cynics on Teesside, used to years of underachievement, have been predicting the three Rs for their team for some time -- runners-up twice (in the league and F.A. Cups) plus relegation.

On Saturday the forecast came true and now the reckoning has arrived. While Chelsea can look forward to European competition, Middlesbrough begin the inevitable dispersal with Juninho, Emerson and Fabrizio Ravanelli top of the departure list.

Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid, Lazio from Italy, Manchester United and Newcastle United are all reported to be interested in Juninho whose brilliance and commitment to Middlesbrough have been a beacon to those around him.
Serious talking is expected this week with some sort of leasing arrangement with Manchester United a possibility.

United and Middlesbrough managers Alex Ferguson and Bryan Robson go back a long way together and one scenario envisages Juninho spending just a season with United and then returning to Middlesbrough if the club wins promotion straight back into the premier league.

Another suggestion is a return to Middlesbrough for United's central defender Gary Pallister with Juninho becoming a permanent feature at Old Trafford where European football is virtually certain for some seasons to come.
Juninho was quoted in one Sunday newspaper as saying it would be "wonderful" to play for United and describing them as the greatest team in England.

Ravanelli, who limped off after 22 minutes on Saturday, looks more likely to return to Italy, with AC Milan thought to be leading the pack, although Liverpool have been impressed by the 31 goals he notched up for Middlesbrough and are said to be able meet his formidable wage bill.
Emerson, a huge disappointment in recent weeks, is more of a problem. One television commentator described his performance on Saturday as "anonymous" and that was being kind.
Few, if any, English clubs will have been impressed and Portugal or Brazil may be the answer for this most enigmatic of players.
While Middlesbrough's foreign contingent prepare to pack their bags, life is all sweetness and light for Chelsea.

Roberto di Matteo's 43rd-second goal was a stunner and helped to earn him the man of the match award. Gianfranco Zola was not at his brilliant best but skilfully laid on the final pass for the second goal which had been initiated by Romanian Dan Petrescu, who had an excellent match.
At the heart of the defence, Frenchman Frank Leboeuf was a solid figure, ensuring that Middlesbrough had few serious efforts on goal.

Chelsea can look forward to the bright lights of Europe while Middlesbrough now contemplate visits to such teams as Tranmere, Port Vale and Oxford -- with time to reflect that maybe that money cannot buy everything.
